sources.title: Signed graphs
sources.citation: Thomas Zaslavsky, Discrete Applied Mathematics 4 (1982), 47-74, Theorem 8B.1 and Corollary 8B.3.
sources.notes: Primary PDF read at Section 8A-8B. Theorem 8B.1 identifies signed-incidence dependencies over rings where 2 is not a zero divisor; Corollary 8B.3 states the field kernel matroid and separates characteristic 2.

nodes.label: Solver-visible yield is at most mathematical yield; completeness gives equality (Lean)
nodes.statement: For a finite decomposition map and any solver/filter predicate, the visible fibre is a subset of the mathematical fibre, so visible yield is at most mathematical yield target by target. Pointwise completeness makes the two fibres equal.
nodes.scope: Finite semantic map with a sound filtering interpretation. Does not prove that a production algebraic solver is sound or complete.

formal.notes: Lean 4.34.1 full build, axiom audit and repository proof gate passed locally.

nodes.label: 'Equal conserved mean determines target-wise yield shape'
nodes.statement: Overbroad bridge: two decomposition maps with the same domain and codomain sizes, hence the same conserved mean, must have the same coverage, zero mass or target-wise counts.
nodes.scope: Refuted by two maps Bool -> Bool with equal total yield and different coverage/fibres.

nodes.label: Equal total yield, different coverage and fibres (Lean countermodel)
nodes.statement: The constant-false and identity maps Bool -> Bool both have total yield 2, but their coverage is 1 versus 2 and their yield at true is 0 versus 1.
nodes.scope: Finite implication countermodel only; not a model of a natural elliptic-curve factor base.

nodes.label: 'Mathematical decomposition yield automatically equals solver-visible yield'
nodes.statement: Overbroad bridge: without a completeness hypothesis, a production solver/filter exposes every mathematical decomposition.
nodes.scope: Refuted by a reject-all filter on the Boolean identity map; production solvers require separate soundness/completeness evidence.

nodes.label: Reject-all solver hides a real decomposition (Lean countermodel)
nodes.statement: For the identity map on Bool, false has mathematical yield 1 while a reject-all solver/filter reports visible yield 0.
nodes.scope: Completeness implication countermodel only; it does not assert that a named solver rejects all witnesses.

nodes.label: 'Success-only retention preserves the failure distribution'
nodes.statement: Overbroad bridge: a population obtained by retaining successful outcomes only can still establish the original failure mass.
nodes.scope: Refuted by the complete Boolean population; it motivates retention of every terminal outcome.

nodes.label: Success-only selection erases a real failure (Lean countermodel)
nodes.statement: The complete Boolean population has one failure, while filtering to successes leaves zero observed failures.
nodes.scope: Finite selection countermodel; it does not quantify the bias of a named adaptive stopping rule.

nodes.label: An unused relation column gives a nonzero right-kernel vector (Lean)
nodes.statement: Over any field, if one column of a finite relation matrix is zero in every row, its coordinate vector is a nonzero right-kernel vector; reusable full-column-rank recovery is impossible.
nodes.scope: Exact support obstruction; it does not assert that a natural population has an unused column.

formal.notes: Lean 4.34.1 full build, axiom audit and repository proof gate passed locally.

nodes.label: 'More rows than columns implies reusable full-column rank'
nodes.statement: Overbroad bridge: an n-by-B relation matrix with n>B has trivial right kernel and therefore uniquely determines a reusable factor-base table.
nodes.scope: Refuted by the zero matrix; row surplus does guarantee a nonzero left kernel, a different condition.

nodes.label: Row surplus with nonzero left and right kernels (Lean countermodel)
nodes.statement: For every B>0 over a field, the (B+1)-by-B zero matrix has a nonzero left-kernel vector by the existing theorem and an explicit nonzero right-kernel vector.
nodes.scope: Implication countermodel only; no claim that natural relation matrices are zero.

nodes.label: Unsigned relation incidence has the even-cycle matroid over odd scalar fields
nodes.statement: For the unsigned edge-vertex incidence matrix over a field of characteristic not two, a connected bipartite component has rank |V|-1 and a connected non-bipartite component has rank |V|. Its left-nullity is therefore |E|-|V|+1 or |E|-|V| respectively; a lone even cycle is dependent and a lone odd cycle is independent.
nodes.scope: Two-nonzero endpoint rows with unsigned +1 coefficients. Signed/folded rows require the corresponding balanced-cycle signature; characteristic two has the ordinary graphic matroid instead.
assumptions: Rows are the declared signed or unsigned incidence representation

nodes.label: 'Any first graph cycle closes two-summand elimination over an odd scalar field'
nodes.statement: Overbroad bridge: the first graph-theoretic cycle in an unsigned two-summand relation graph always gives a nonzero left-kernel vector.
nodes.scope: Refuted by a triangle over F_3. The valid replacement is a balanced/even-circuit condition plus a nonzero target projection.

nodes.label: Triangle and self-pair loop need not close unsigned elimination over F3 (Lean)
nodes.statement: The three unsigned incidence rows of a triangle have only the zero left-kernel vector over F_3, although the graph already contains a cycle. A self-pair loop row has coefficient 2 and is likewise independent.
nodes.scope: Finite implication countermodels. The triangle determinant and loop coefficient are 2, so both obstructions hold over every odd prime field; the Lean owner instantiates F_3.

nodes.label: Square and parallel-edge circuits give unsigned row dependencies over F3 (Lean)
nodes.statement: Alternating weights cancel the unsigned incidence rows of a square, and opposite weights cancel two parallel rows. These are positive controls for an even simple cycle and a length-two multigraph cycle.
nodes.scope: Finite F_3 controls, not a stopping-time law for a natural relation stream.

nodes.label: A row dependency recovers the target only with nonzero target projection (Lean)
nodes.statement: After factor-base cancellation, a weighted scalar equation A+B*d=0 determines the target logarithm as d=-A/B when B is nonzero. If B=0, the graph dependency alone can be uninformative.
nodes.scope: Exact field-algebra bridge. It does not establish the distribution or nonvanishing probability of B in a natural relation process.
assumptions: Nonzero weighted target coefficient for recovery

nodes.label: M31 natural stream: first useful balanced circuit at 97 exact-two-LP edges for K=168
nodes.statement: On one fixed source-ordered M31 prefix with declared large-prime pool K=168, the first ordinary graph cycle, balanced circuit, exact LP dependency, nonzero target projection and projected-rank increase coincide at exact-two-LP edge 97 (source position 457). Its target coefficient is 744325019 modulo 2147446831. Exact target uniqueness is not observed by the 512-admitted-row censor.
nodes.scope: One retained stream and one K. The fixed ten-query collection boundary was independent of the measured events, but complete probe/reject custody is unavailable. This is an unsigned repository measurement, not an asymptotic exponent, concentration law, complete-cost result or ECDLP speedup. [pcc:unverified]
assumptions: The retained source-order prefix represents the producer's admitted order
Arithmetic is over the declared prime scalar field

nodes.label: Two-summand useful balanced-circuit stopping law
nodes.statement: For the route's exact signed multigraph process, prove or measure without stopping bias the accepted-edge stopping law rho(K) for the first balanced circuit whose weighted target coefficient is nonzero. Determine whether rho(K) is concentrated, its power-law exponent if any, and whether the former rho(K)=K/2 specialization is conservative.
nodes.scope: The deterministic incidence algebra is closed and one K=168 retained stream now gives rho(168)=97, with target uniqueness still absent at the censor. What remains is a preregistered multi-K, multi-seed natural edge/sign ensemble establishing useful-circuit concentration and scaling, target projection and repeated-target exclusion; this is distinct from reusable right/full-rank tables.

edges.statement: Equal conserved totals coexist with different coverage and target fibres.
A target-wise law needs hypotheses beyond the conserved mean.
Coverage can change while the mean is fixed.
Visible yield is bounded above by mathematical yield and equals it only with a completeness certificate.
A reject-all filter hides an existing witness.
Mathematical enumeration alone cannot certify production-solver completeness.
Success-only filtering erases the failure mass.
A complete terminal manifest is necessary to distinguish zero, failure and rejection.
An unused column is an exact obstruction to reusable full-column rank.
Terminal rank requires support of every reusable column, not only a row surplus.
A surplus-row matrix can have nonzero left and right kernels simultaneously.
Row count alone does not discharge the reusable rank heuristic.
Left-kernel existence and right-kernel uniqueness are distinct obligations.
The displayed r^(1/6) family law specializes the unresolved useful-circuit stopping law to rho(K)=K/2; it is not a reusable full-rank condition.
A triangle is a cycle but its unsigned incidence rows are independent over F_3.
Over an odd scalar field the relevant incidence circuits are balanced; an arbitrary first cycle is insufficient.
Even and parallel-edge circuits are finite positive controls, but do not determine their natural arrival time.
A balanced incidence circuit closes target elimination only when its weighted target coefficient is nonzero.
One uncensored retained stream supplies rho(168)=97 and separates useful-circuit arrival from target uniqueness; multiple K and seeds are still required for a stopping law.
The first balanced circuit in the exact-two-LP panel has a nonzero weighted target coefficient.
The single observation 97 > K/2 = 84 does not validate the rho(K)=K/2 specialization or any asymptotic improvement.
